transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I go from feeling like I can work nonstop and take on everything to suddenly having no energy to even show up for my shifts. My manager at the restaurant and my mom both noticed these dramatic changes and got really worried, which is why I reluctantly agreed to come in today.
Can you tell me more about how long these periods of high energy and low energy typically last, and how often you experience these shifts in mood?

This whole back-and-forth cycle has been going on for about four months in total, starting when I began working extra double shifts. The initial high-energy phase lasted about a month, but this heavy, low stretch where I can barely get myself to work has been hanging over me for around three months now.
During these periods of high energy, do you experience any symptoms like excessive spending, risky behaviors, or decreased need for sleep?

I definitely experienced a decreased need for sleep—I'd stay up all night sketching business plans or deep-cleaning my apartment at 3 a.m. while insisting I didn't need rest. I don't really recall doing any risky behaviors or excessive spending during those high times, though I do have some older credit card debt from dropping out of college.

Can you describe your mood and thoughts during these low-energy periods, such as feeling sad, hopeless, or worthless, and have you experienced any changes in appetite or interest in activities you normally enjoy?

During these low stretches, I feel completely wiped out and have lost interest in things I used to love, like playing Sunday soccer and cooking, so I mostly just sit and scroll on my phone. My appetite is also all over the place—I either forget to eat all day or suddenly inhale a whole pizza at midnight, and my clothes are starting to hang loose on me.
Do you often feel guilty, worthless, or have thoughts that you're a burden to others during these low-energy periods?

No, I haven't really felt guilty, worthless, or like I'm a burden to others, even when my energy is at its lowest. It's more just a feeling of being completely drained and physically unable to get things done.
Can you tell me if, during your high-energy periods, you ever felt irritable or if your mood was more elevated and expansive, and did these mood changes occur in distinct episodes?

During those high-energy times, my mood would flip between feeling on top of the world—cracking jokes and hugging coworkers—to suddenly snapping at people over tiny things like a messed-up ticket. It definitely happened in distinct phases; that unstoppable, high-energy month completely gave way to this heavy, low stretch that has been dragging on for the past three months.

Can you clarify if you've had any periods of stability in your mood, where you felt relatively normal and not extremely high or low in energy, between these episodes or at any point in the past four months?

No, I haven't really had any periods of feeling normal or stable over these past four months. I went straight from that first month of feeling completely unstoppable right into this heavy, low stretch that I've been stuck in for the last three months, with absolutely no middle ground in between.
Have you experienced any episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that lasted for at least one week, but less than two weeks, in addition to your described high-energy periods?

No, I haven't experienced any separate high or irritable periods that lasted just one or two weeks. That main high phase I talked about lasted for about a month straight before I transitioned into this current low stretch.

Can you confirm if your high-energy period, which lasted about a month, was characterized by an abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood, and if this was clearly distinct from your normal mood?

Yes, during that first month, my mood was completely different from my normal self, and the change was very obvious. I would constantly flip between feeling on top of the world—cracking jokes and planning multiple businesses—to suddenly snapping at my coworkers over tiny things.
During either your high-energy or low-energy periods, have you ever experienced any break from reality, such as hearing voices or seeing things that weren't there?
No, I've never experienced anything like that. I haven't heard voices, seen things that weren't there, or had any other breaks from reality during either my high or low periods.
Have you experienced any recurring thoughts of death, suicidal ideation, or attempts to harm yourself during these low-energy periods?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself, suicide, or death, even when I've felt at my absolute lowest. It's really just been a struggle with feeling completely drained of energy.

You mentioned you haven't experienced any breaks from reality, but can you confirm if you've ever had any fleeting or suspicious thoughts that might seem unusual or out of character for you during either your high or low periods?
No, I haven't really experienced any suspicious, paranoid, or unusual thoughts like that. Even when my mood is extremely high or very low, my thoughts have never gone in that direction.
Have you noticed any seasonal patterns or correlations with specific events that seem to trigger these shifts between high-energy and low-energy periods?

I haven't noticed any seasonal patterns, but the shifts definitely started when I began picking up extra double shifts at the restaurant. Dealing with late nights, irregular meals, and a chaotic schedule to save for a trip and pay off credit card debt is what really seemed to trigger it.
Can you describe if your high-energy periods were always followed by low-energy periods, or if there were instances where you went back to a high-energy state after a low-energy period?

So far, I've only gone through this one cycle. I had that high-energy period that lasted for about a month, which then crashed into this heavy, low-energy stretch I've been stuck in for the past three months. I haven't gone back to a high-energy state at all since this low period started.

Can you confirm if your current low-energy period, which has lasted for about three months, has been a single, continuous episode or if there have been any brief periods where your mood and energy returned to normal or near-normal before dropping again?

Yes, it has been completely continuous. This heavy feeling has been hanging over me every single day for the entire three months without any breaks where my energy or mood returned to normal. It hasn't let up at all.

Can you clarify if, during your high-energy month, you experienced at least three of the following symptoms: inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, flight of ideas, distractibility, increase in goal-directed activity, or excessive involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences?

Yes, I definitely experienced several of those symptoms during that high stretch. I felt so confident that I was convinced I could run my own restaurant chain, and my mind would race with a million ideas while I talked so fast people couldn't get a word in. I also stayed up all night working on food truck plans without needing sleep and constantly took on extra shifts.
Did you experience any periods where you felt a mix of both high and low symptoms at the same time, or did these episodes always occur separately?

No, they definitely occurred separately rather than at the same time. First, I had that big "up" streak where I felt completely unstoppable and worked nonstop, and then that gave way to the heavy, low stretch I've been stuck in for the last three months.

Can you confirm if your high-energy period, which lasted about a month, included a distinct period where your mood was abnormally elevated or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Yes, absolutely. For that entire month, I was either feeling completely on top of the world or snapping at people over the tiniest things almost every single day. It was a constant, intense state that lasted the whole four weeks before I finally crashed into this low period.

Can you confirm if the entire duration of your high-energy period, which lasted about a month, was characterized by an abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood, and if this period was not interrupted by any return to normal mood or a depressive episode?

Yes, I can confirm that. For that entire first month, my mood was constantly either on top of the world or extremely irritable, with absolutely no breaks or return to normal. It wasn't until after that full month ended that I finally crashed into this three-month low period.
Can you confirm if your high-energy period, which lasted about a month, met the full criteria for a manic episode, including lasting at least one week, or if it fell short of this duration?
Yes, it definitely lasted much longer than a single week. It was a solid month of me feeling completely unstoppable and working nonstop before the crash finally happened.

Can you confirm if your current three-month low-energy period has included at least five of the following symptoms: depressed mood most of the day, markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities, significant weight loss or gain, insomnia or hypersomnia, psychomotor agitation or retardation, fatigue or loss of energy, feelings of worthlessness or guilt, diminished ability to think or concentrate, or recurrent thoughts of death?

Yes, I've definitely experienced most of those symptoms during this heavy three-month low stretch. I've completely lost interest in soccer and cooking, my appetite and weight are swinging wildly, and I have this deep fatigue that sleep doesn't help. Plus, my brain is so foggy that I forget simple orders at work, and I alternate between feeling like I'm moving through mud and pacing restlessly.

Can you further clarify if there were any periods within your high-energy month where your mood was not elevated or irritable, or if the entire month was consistently marked by these symptoms without any breaks?
I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it in that much detail, but looking back, it just felt like one big, continuous blur of being wound up.

Can you confirm if your high-energy period, which lasted about a month, was preceded by or followed by a major depressive episode, and if so, did the depressive episode occur immediately after the manic episode?

Yes, my high-energy period lasted for about a month and was immediately followed by this heavy, low stretch. The transition happened about three months ago, right after that month-long burst of overworking myself, which led straight into the prolonged downturn I'm experiencing now.
Can you confirm if your high-energy period was the first episode you experienced, or if you had any previous episodes of either high or low energy before this current cycle began?

Yes, this is the very first time I've ever experienced these extreme high and low periods. It all started about four months ago when I began taking on all those extra double shifts at the restaurant to save money. Before that, my mood and energy were always pretty normal and steady.
Can you confirm if your current diagnosis could be better described as having distinct episodes of mania and depression, or if the symptoms have been more persistent and overlapping?

Yes, they’ve definitely been distinct, separate phases rather than overlapping. I had that initial month where I felt completely unstoppable and worked nonstop, which then totally flipped into this prolonged low phase of feeling drained and depressed for the last three months.

Can you confirm if the depressive episode that followed your manic episode lasted for at least two weeks, and if it was characterized by a consistently depressed mood for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, it has lasted much longer than two weeks, as this heavy, low stretch has been going on consistently for about three months now. During this entire time, I've felt drained and low nearly every single day, making it incredibly hard to even get myself to work or handle basic tasks around my apartment.

Can you confirm if your manic episode, which lasted about a month, was immediately followed by a major depressive episode without any period of normal mood in between, and has this pattern been consistent throughout the four months you've been experiencing these mood swings?

Yes, that's exactly how it happened. I went straight from that month-long high phase right into this low phase without any period of normal mood in between. This low stretch has now lasted for about three months, which fits the total four months I've been dealing with this.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any other episodes of mania or depression before this current cycle, and if so, how they compare in terms of duration and symptoms to the episodes you've described?

No, I haven't had any other episodes before this. This is the very first time I've ever experienced these kinds of extreme ups and downs, and my mood was completely stable before this cycle started four months ago.
